item.text: With lint clean, I’ll move to a design cleanup: `Simulator` currently stores real actor instances as spawn-probability keys, which places temporary actors in the field just to describe spawning. I’m replacing that with spawn rules/factories so population setup no longer relies on prototype actors.
I’m adding a terrain check overload to `Field` so spawn rules can ask about land/water capability without manufacturing an actor first. Then `Simulator` can hold pure spawn rules.
The field overload is in place. I’m replacing `Map<Actor, Double>` with an ordered list of spawn rules and constructor references, removing the prototype actors entirely.
`Simulator` now has spawn rules instead of prototype actors. I’m compiling and linting to catch any constructor-reference or type issues.
Compile and full lint are clean. I’m reviewing the diff now, with special attention to population behavior and spawn-rule ordering.

item.text:
Refactor pass complete.

Main change: `Simulator` no longer creates temporary “prototype” actors just to store spawn probabilities. It now uses explicit `ActorCreationRule` entries with constructor references, so initial population setup is data-driven and does not mutate the field before `reset()`.

Also added a `Field.canOccupy(boolean canMoveOnLand, boolean canMoveOnWater, Location)` overload so spawn rules can check terrain compatibility without needing an actor instance.

Validation:
- `javac *.java` passes.
- `javac -Xlint:all *.java` passes with no warnings.
